transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because, well, I've started planning my days around not using elevators. It's just getting to be a real hassle. 

I've been taking five flights of stairs every day at my apartment building. I even turned down a training workshop recently because it was in a high-rise. And I actually had to stop doing home visits with one of my older computer students because his building doesn't really have another option besides the elevator. So, yeah, I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When you imagine riding an elevator, what specifically are you afraid might happen?

Well, I know an elevator in a modern office block is probably safe. But when I look at those old doors in my apartment building, or even at some of the buildings I visit for work, my mind just... it treats it like I’m about to get trapped inside. Or like the whole thing is just going to drop. Part of me knows that sounds pretty over the top, but that's exactly what I picture happening.
Do you also fear or avoid other situations where you might feel unable to escape or get help, such as crowded places, public transportation, or being outside alone?

No, not really. I don't have any issues with crowds or taking the bus or anything like that. Being outside alone is totally fine for me, too. It really is just... just the elevators that give me this problem.
